study_identification_part.si4_title: Investigating dopaminergic abnormalities in schizophrenia and first-episode psychosis with normative modelling and multisite molecular neuroimaging

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study explicitly states its primary objective to demonstrate the feasibility of employing normative modeling for molecular neuroimaging in schizophrenia and psychotic disorders. It outlines specific hypotheses, including identifying spatial patterns of molecular alterations, comparing findings across datasets, and linking deviations to clinical symptoms and treatment response.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: In this work, our primary objective is to demonstrate the feasibility of employing normative modelling for molecular neuroimaging in SCZ and psychotic disorders. ... We hypothesise that normative modelling can be effectively applied to this type of data... Furthermore, we hypothesise that normative modelling can serve as a powerful tool to identify both the magnitude and the spatial distribution of molecular alterations... and linking inter-individual deviation from normalities to clinical symptoms and response to treatment.
